purpose: Provide a citizen-facing, evidence-backed explanation of who was involved in an approved property event, the role supported by evidence, the affected property interest, relevant date and explicit limits.
core_principle: PERSON/ORGANISATION → DOCUMENT/EVENT ROLE → PROPERTY INTEREST → DATE → LEGAL BASIS → LIMITATION
rules: A person's appearance in a document does not by itself establish ownership or another property interest.
A party role and a property-interest role are kept distinct until evidence connects them.
Registered proprietor, beneficial owner, personal representative, mortgagee, tenant and occupier are not interchangeable.
Party identity requires sufficient matching evidence; similar names are not silently merged.
The role is time-bounded and cannot automatically be projected to another date.
A person may have multiple distinct roles in one event or across different events.
Role resolution retains the property and event match.
Citizen-supplied assertions remain assertions until validated.
Only necessary personal information is displayed publicly.
Unresolved role or identity conflicts remain visible.
hard_stops: Never infer ownership from document participation alone.
Never infer beneficial ownership from registered title alone.
Never infer personal ownership from personal-representative status.
Never infer mortgagee/charge-holder status from a person's name without matching evidence.
Never merge similar names without identity evidence.
Never project a current role backward without historical evidence.
Never turn role association into a new legal conclusion during display.
